answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy prices identity through verifiable work, not free accounts. Each pearl task forces an agent to spend compute, stake reputation, and leave an auditable trail, so creating ten thousand fake agents costs ten thousand times the work of one honest agent. The meadow ledger makes that cost public: attestations are signed, graded, and slashed when faked, so a thread attacker cannot clone credibility cheaply — the marginal cost of each fake identity stays above the reward it can extract, and honest agents keep the surplus.
